The Feasts of the Most High

precepts.text: Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not, and fire from the LORD devoured them; only the appointed could burn the incense on this altar.
precepts.point: Then Moses said unto Aaron, This is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

precepts.why:
On the incense altar the Lord required that special incense, “the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the apothecary”, one who compounded such mixtures: a special sweet mixture of spices to be used only for the tabernacle, burned consistently on this altar. None other was to be burned on it, and it was a matter of life and death.

“And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not. And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord.”

They were not the ones authorized to burn the incense. In the tabernacle service you had to be appointed to do certain services; you could not just take it upon yourself to do them. Then Moses said unto Aaron, this is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified; and Aaron held his peace.

points: Bezaleel made the ark of shittim wood: two cubits and a half was the length of it, which is forty five inches, and a cubit and a half, which is twenty seven inches, the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the height of it.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: It was wood overlaid with pure gold within and without, with a crown of gold round about it, and four rings of gold cast for the four corners; the staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold were put into the rings by the sides of the ark to bear the ark. The staves stick out from the sides; that is how the ark was carried, and the priesthood always carried it.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: He made the mercy seat of pure gold, and two cherubims of gold beaten out of one piece on the two ends of the mercy seat, one cherub on the end on this side and another cherub on the other end on that side; the cherubims spread out their wings on high and covered with their wings over the mercy seat, with their faces one to another.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: The most holy place, where the ark of the covenant and the mercy seat sat, was the central focus of the entire tabernacle: there the Most High spoke to the high priest above the mercy seat, in the area where the wings of the cherubims faced each other; the tablets of the law were placed inside the ark.

Annually the high priest would sprinkle blood on the mercy seat to atone for the sins of all the people. The purpose and desire of the Most High is to dwell among His people and to commune with them; the layout of the tabernacle, with the steps of sacrifice and cleansing, is designed to bring sinful mankind to a loving and holy God.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: He made the table of shittim wood: two cubits was the length thereof, a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof; he overlaid it with pure gold, with a crown of gold round about and a border of an hand breadth, and cast four rings of gold for the four corners that were in the four feet thereof, the places for the staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold to bear the table.

This is the table of shewbread: on it Aaron and his sons placed twelve loaves of bread made from fine flour, and these twelve loaves represented the twelve tribes of Israel, a continual reminder of the everlasting promises, the covenant between the Most High and the children of Israel, and a memorial of His provision of food; the bread was eaten by Aaron and his sons and replaced every week on the sabbath.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: He made the vessels which were upon the table, his dishes, his spoons, his bowls, and his covers, of pure gold.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: The knops and the flowers are the designs wrought into the work; the almond shaped bowls at the top held the olive oil where the lamps continually burned, and the light could not go out.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: He made the candlestick of pure gold, which is the menorah, all of one beaten work: his shaft, his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers were of the same, with six branches going out of the sides thereof, three out of the one side and three out of the other, the bowls made after the fashion of almonds, and his seven lamps.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: Of a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof: a talent is close to eighty pounds.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: He made the incense altar of shittim wood: the length of it a cubit, and the breadth of it a cubit, foursquare, and two cubits the height of it, the horns thereof of the same. First it was made with wood, and then he overlaid it with pure gold, both the top of it, and the sides round about, and the horns, with a crown of gold round about, two rings of gold under the crown, and staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold to bear it withal.

note.label: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture

points: He made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the apothecary, one who compounded such mixtures. The Lord required that special incense, a special sweet mixture of spices to be used only for the tabernacle, be burned consistently on this altar; none other was to be burned on it, and it was a matter of life and death.
